requirements.name: Message Parameter / Serial Number

cases.case: Serial number is a 16-bit value altered per message
cases.what: The serial number is a 16-bit value that changes for every new warning of the same message identifier.

cases.case: Geographical scope indicator
cases.what: The code does not set the geographical scope bits; they stay zero until the counter passes 16383.

cases.case: Location Area wide scope in GSM
cases.what: The code does not set a geographical scope and has no GSM side.

cases.case: Service Area wide scope in UMTS
cases.what: The code does not set a geographical scope and has no UMTS side.

cases.case: Update number increments by 1 for each update
cases.what: The low four bits of a flat per-type counter act as the update number and increment by one per warning, but after 15 the carry changes the message code and there is no separate update concept; the first value is 1, not 0000.

noted: It is one plain counter per alert type, not split into geographical scope, message code and update number.

requirements.name: CBC Functionality

cases.case: CBC connected to several BSC/RNC/MME/PWS-IWF
cases.what: The CBC connects to one configured MME endpoint; it has no list of MMEs and no BSC, RNC or PWS-IWF interface.

cases.case: CBC connected to several CBEs
cases.what: The HTTP API serves any number of originators at once; each names itself in the sender field.

cases.case: Allocation of serial numbers
cases.what: The CBC allocates the 16-bit serial number of each warning from a per-alert-type counter that wraps at 65536.

cases.case: Deleting CBS messages held by the eNodeB
cases.what: A Stop-Warning-Request naming the message identifier and serial number is sent to the MME on request.

cases.case: Modifying CBS messages held by the eNodeB
cases.what: A new warning of the same alert type is sent with the same Message Identifier and the next serial number, so it can replace the earlier one at the network.

cases.case: Initiating broadcast by sending the CBS message to the RAN
cases.what: The CBC sends one Write-Replace-Warning-Request to the MME bridge whose Warning Message Content is the unpaged GSM 7-bit packed text; it builds no 82-octet CBS-Message-Information-Pages, no Number-of-Pages or length octets (TS 23.041 9.3.35, 9.3.19), and no message per language.

cases.case: Padding pages to 82 octets
cases.what: The message text is packed once into a single octet string; no page structure is built and nothing is padded to 82 octets.

cases.case: One message for each language of the cell
cases.what: Only one message in one language is sent per warning; there is no per-language handling.

cases.case: Determining the set of cells
cases.what: The CBC sends no cell list, tracking area list or warning area list; the area is left to the MME, or given only as area coordinates when the originator draws shapes.

cases.case: Geographical scope in the Serial Number
cases.what: The serial number is a plain counter; the geographical scope bits are not set from the warning area.

cases.case: Determining the start time of broadcast
cases.what: A warning is sent as soon as the request is accepted; no start time can be set or scheduled.

cases.case: Determining the time to cease broadcast
cases.what: The CBC sets no end time; a warning stays until the operator stops it or the number of broadcasts requested is used up.

cases.case: Instructing the network to cease broadcast
cases.what: On request the CBC sends a Stop-Warning-Request for a named warning, or for the most recent active one.

cases.case: Determining the repetition period
cases.what: The repetition period comes from the request, with 4096 seconds as the default, and is sent in the Repetition Period IE.

cases.case: Cell broadcast channel in GSM
cases.what: The condition is not met: the CBC serves LTE through SBc-AP only and chooses no GSM cell broadcast channel.

cases.case: Lists of cells towards the BSC/RNC
cases.what: The condition is not met: the CBC has no BSC or RNC interface and sends no cell lists.

cases.case: The CBC shall be responsible for the management of CBS messages including:
cases.what: The CBC manages the lifecycle of the messages it sends in part (allocates serial numbers, writes and stops warnings, passes repetition period) but not as clause 5 describes: serial number has no geographical scope or update number, no padding to 82 octets, no cell determination, no start and stop time determination.

cases.case: - when CBS transmits emergency messages, allocation of "emergency indication" to ...
cases.what: The CBC sets a Warning Type (ETWS types only) and the warning message content, and the test alert type exists, but it sends no Cell ID or TAI list or Warning Area List and never sets an emergency indication beyond the message identifier range.

noted: A single endpoint string is used for every request (, 290, 354).
All originators share one credential.
The counter is a plain count held in memory (restarts after a service restart); it does not build the geographical scope, message code and update number fields of the serial number.
There is no separate modify operation; replacement happens by sending a new warning of the same type.
The request goes to the MME, not directly to an eNodeB.
The default and the highest accepted value, 4096, are above the 4095 that TS 29.168 allows a current CBC to send.
